title: Frigidaire vs. Honeywell Dehumidifier (2026): Which to Buy?
dek: Both say "50" on the box. Only one of them removes 50 pints a day — but the other has the better lab score.
description: Frigidaire vs. Honeywell dehumidifier: the FHDD5034Y1 and TPFIT50AWK compared on real DOE capacity, test scores, warranty, makers and recall history.
intro: The Frigidaire vs. Honeywell dehumidifier matchup looks even at first glance. Each brand's popular Wi-Fi model carries a "50" in its name, both connect to Alexa, and both back their compressors with five years of sealed-system coverage. Look closer and they turn out to be very different machines from very different supply chains.

The biggest surprise is capacity. Frigidaire's **FHDD5034Y1** is rated at a genuine 50 pints a day under the current 2019 DOE test. Honeywell's **TPFIT50AWK** keeps a model name from the pre-2019 rating scale and is rated at roughly 32 pints a day under today's test — about a third less water, usually at a higher price. Honeywell's counterpunch is a strong independent score: Consumer Reports gave it an 88 and ranked it first among the large-capacity models it rated.
We compared the two using DOE ratings, manufacturer specs and warranty terms, published independent scores and the CPSC recall database. We don't run our own lab tests.
topPicksLead: For most shoppers, the **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1** is the better buy because it removes more water for less money; the **Honeywell TPFIT50AWK** makes sense if a top independent score matters more than raw capacity.

blocks.text: We matched each brand's closest current Wi-Fi flagship and compared them on capacity under the 2019 DOE procedure, manufacturer spec sheets for coverage, drainage and low-temperature operation, and published warranty terms. We added independent scores where they exist, checked the CPSC recall database for both brand names and read owner reviews for patterns around reliability and service. We do not lab-test dehumidifiers.

sections.heading: The naming gap: why a Honeywell "50" isn't 50 pints

blocks.text: In 2019, the Department of Energy lowered its dehumidifier test temperature from 80°F to 65°F. Cooler air gives up less water, so every unit's rating dropped by roughly 30%. Frigidaire renamed its models to match the new figures. Honeywell kept its old names, so its model numbers still describe pre-2019 capacity.

items: **Honeywell TPFIT50AWK:** "50" in the name, about 32 pints under today's test.
**Honeywell TP70 series:** "70" in the name, about 50 pints under today's test — the true match for the Frigidaire.
**Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1:** "50" in the name, 50 pints under today's test.

blocks.title: Shopping tip
blocks.text: Ignore the number in any model name and look for the DOE 2019 rating on the spec sheet or EnergyGuide label. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) explains how much capacity your space needs.

sections.heading: Who makes them, and their recall histories

blocks.text: Neither brand builds its own dehumidifiers. Frigidaire's current units come from a licensed manufacturer in Midea's family, the same group behind several other brands we cover. Honeywell's are made by JMATEK, which has operated as Honeywell Air Comfort since 2014 — an entirely separate supply chain.

Both names appear in old fire-hazard recalls, but from unrelated manufacturers. Frigidaire was one of 13 brands on a Gree-built platform recalled in 2013 and reannounced in 2016 after roughly 450 fires. Honeywell-branded units built by New Widetech (models DH45W, DH50W and DH70W) were among about 20 brands recalled in 2021 after more than 100 overheating and fire incidents. Neither recall covers the current models compared here, but always check a secondhand unit's model number and date code at CPSC.gov.

For most homes, the **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1** is the smarter purchase: it's a genuine 50-pint dehumidifier that usually costs less than the Honeywell. The **Honeywell TPFIT50AWK** earns its place with a Consumer Reports score of 88, but it removes about a third less water under the current test. Whichever brand you lean toward, compare dehumidifiers on their DOE 2019 rating, never on the number in the model name.

faqs.q: Is Frigidaire or Honeywell the better dehumidifier brand?
faqs.a: For capacity per dollar, Frigidaire. Its FHDD5034Y1 removes a genuine 50 pints a day and usually costs less. Honeywell's TPFIT50AWK has the stronger independent score (Consumer Reports 88), but it's rated at only about 32 pints a day under the current DOE test.

faqs.q: Is the Honeywell TPFIT50AWK really a 50-pint dehumidifier?
faqs.a: No. Its name references the pre-2019 rating scale. Under the current DOE test it's rated at roughly 32 pints a day. Honeywell's true 50-pint models are in the TP70 series.

faqs.q: Are Frigidaire and Honeywell dehumidifiers made by the same company?
faqs.a: No. Frigidaire's current dehumidifiers are built under license by a Midea-family manufacturer, while Honeywell's are made by JMATEK, operating as Honeywell Air Comfort. They share no hardware platform.
They're essentially tied: one year on parts and labor plus five years on the sealed refrigeration system. Some reviewers report that Honeywell's out-of-warranty repairs can be slow and costly.

faqs.q: Have Frigidaire or Honeywell dehumidifiers been recalled?
faqs.a: Both brand names appear in older recalls from different manufacturers: Frigidaire in the Gree recall first announced in 2013, and Honeywell-branded New Widetech units in a 2021 recall. Neither affects the current models compared here. Check any used unit at CPSC.gov.
